featured_reviews.name: Sarbjeet Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Naaz Family Restaurant – A Taste of Tradition | ★★★★☆ (4/5)

Humara Naaz, Kurla ka Swad!
Naaz Family Restaurant has been a beloved part of Kurla since 1968 – a true culinary landmark nestled conveniently near Phoenix Market City. Stepping into Naaz feels like stepping into a flavorful legacy passed down through generations.

What I Loved:

Authentic Flavors: Every bite spoke volumes about their time-honored recipes. You can taste the richness and tradition in each dish – it’s clear they've been perfecting their craft for decades.

Warm, Family Atmosphere: Despite the lively crowd, the place radiates warmth. It’s cozy, familiar, and perfect for a wholesome family meal.

Prime Location: Just a stone’s throw from Phoenix Market City, it’s easy to find. Their multiple contact numbers also reflect their efficiency with deliveries and takeaways.

What Could Be Better:

Food Consistency: While most dishes were excellent, I noticed slight variation in quality – possibly due to the high rush hours.

Crowded Seating: The place tends to get packed, especially during peak times. Better space management or a seating upgrade would go a long way.

Ambiance: The decor feels a bit dated. A little refresh could add charm without losing its traditional essence.

Final Thoughts:
If you're looking for authentic, flavorful comfort food served with a side of nostalgia, Naaz Family Restaurant is a must-visit. It’s a true reflection of Mumbai’s culinary heritage, and with a few small tweaks, it could easily shine even brighter.

featured_reviews.name: Rahul Parab
featured_reviews.review_text: Arabian Dastar is a hidden gem for anyone craving authentic Arabian flavors. This cozy yet elegant spot delivers a feast that transports you straight to the heart of the Middle East. If you're in the mood to explore rich, aromatic, and flavorful dishes, this restaurant is your destination. From appetizers to desserts, Dastar offers an unforgettable experience with its menu full of traditional favorites. Here's a glimpse of what we tried and why you should too. The evening kicked off with a warm, comforting bowl of Shorba, a classic Arabian soup that sets the tone for the meal ahead. The broth was perfectly spiced, with delicate notes of cumin and cinnamon. With each spoonful, you could taste the depth of flavor and the smooth, velvety texture that only comes from hours of careful simmering. Served hot, it was the ideal starter, warming us up and preparing our palates for the upcoming dishes. Next up was the showstopper: the Turkey Roast Chicken. A twist on the traditional roasted chicken, this dish used turkey, marinated in a blend of Arabian spices and herbs. The turkey was tender, juicy, and roasted to perfection, its skin crisped to a beautiful golden-brown. The seasoning was a perfect balance of savory and aromatic, with hints of garlic, cumin, and coriander. Paired with a side of fresh vegetables and rice, this was a hearty and satisfying main course that stood out for its delicate yet bold flavors. If you're looking for a dish that embodies the soul of Arabian cuisine, the Omani Mandi is a must-try. This traditional rice dish is packed with flavor, where tender lamb (or chicken) is cooked with rice, saffron, and a blend of spices. At Dastar, the Mandi was perfectly cooked, with each grain of rice soaked in the rich, fragrant broth. The lamb was succulent, falling off the bone with ease. The dish was an aromatic masterpiece, with a hint of smokiness that comes from the traditional cooking method. It's a dish that speaks to the heart of Arabian comfort food. To wrap up our meal, we indulged in a classic Arabian dessert: Kunafa. This popular sweet is made from delicate strands of semolina dough, soaked in sugar syrup, and topped with melted cheese or cream. At Dastar, the Kunafa was served warm and gooey, with the perfect balance of sweetness and richness. The texture was spot-on: crispy on the outside and melt-in-your-mouth soft on the inside. The fragrant rosewater and the syrup provided just the right touch of sweetness, making it an unforgettable finish to the meal. Dastar Restaurant delivers an authentic Arabian dining experience with impeccable service and a menu that brings the best of the Middle East to your table. Whether you're new to Arabian food or a seasoned fan, their Shorba, Turkey Roast Chicken, Omani Mandi, and Kunafa will leave you craving more. Every dish was a testament to the skillful use of spices, and the flavors were rich, comforting, and full of character. If you're in the area, don't miss the chance to explore the vibrant tastes of Arabian cuisine at Dastar. You won’t be disappointed

featured_reviews.name: Prachi Jaiswal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I usually go to Naveena for parotta and saru, but this time I decided to try this place. Unfortunately, the experience was quite disappointing.

We ordered parotta with saru, masala omelette, chicken biryani, and chicken 65.

The parotta was very rubbery and not enjoyable at all. They serve both chicken and mutton saru, but the taste was below average and the spice level was overwhelming. None of the food we ordered stood out in terms of taste.

The service was extremely slow. We ordered a masala omelette and chicken 65 to have with the parotta, but the omelette was completely forgotten, and the chicken 65 arrived only after we had finished the parotta and biryani.

The chicken biryani was dry, overly spicy, and loaded with too much whole masala (khada masala), which made it difficult to enjoy. The quantity of chicken 65 was also surprisingly small for the price.

Overall, we spent around ₹450 and felt it was not worth it. Between the below-average food, delayed service, and missed items, the experience was disappointing. I wouldn’t recommend this place based on my visit.

Highly recommended for anyone craving real South Tamil Nadu style non-veg food near Chembur.
